title: Novel 3,3'-diindolylmethane derivatives as multi-pathway modulators: targeting estrogen-dependent and independent breast cancer carcinogenesis.
authors: Ince-Erguc, Elif; Entezari, Bita; Sirinzade, Hanif; Suzen, Sibel; Akdemir, Atilla; Erdogan, Oguz; Gurer-Orhan, Hande
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦乳腺癌药物设计与酶抑制活性，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-酶互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: PURPOSE: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women, with prolonged exposure to endogenous estrogens recognized as a major risk factor. This study aimed to design, synthesize, and pharmacologically evaluate novel 3,3'-diindolylmethane (DIM) derivatives as multi-target modulators of estrogen-related pathways in breast cancer. METHODS: A series of DIM derivatives was synthesized and structurally characterized. Their biological activities were assessed through aromatase (CYP19A1) and CYP1B1 inhibition assays, E-screen assay for estrogen receptor activity, cytotoxicity assays in breast cancer (MCF-7 BUS, MDA-MB-231) and normal breast epithelial (MCF-10 A) cells, and scratch assay for cell migration. Molecular docking and in silico ADME analyses were conducted to support experimental findings. RESULTS: The derivatives demonstrated significant antiestrogenic activity by targeting multiple components of estrogen signaling. One compound exhibited potent aromatase inhibition (IC(5)(0) = 0.79 microM), while two derivatives showed strong CYP1B1 inhibition (IC(5)(0) = 0.37 microM and 0.71 microM). Selective cytotoxicity was observed in estrogen receptor-positive cells, with reduced effects on normal cells. Additionally, selected compounds significantly inhibited cell migration. Molecular modeling revealed favorable binding interactions within target enzymes, and ADME analysis indicated acceptable drug-like properties. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that DIM derivatives act as selective, multi-target modulators of estrogen-related pathways and may serve as promising adjuvant candidates for hormone-dependent breast cancer therapy.
abstract_zh: 目的：乳腺癌仍然是女性癌症相关死亡的主要原因，长期暴露于内源性雌激素被认为是主要风险因素。本研究旨在设计、合成并对新型3,3'-二吲哚甲烷（DIM）衍生物进行药理学评价，作为乳腺癌中雌激素相关通路的多靶点调节剂。方法：合成了一系列DIM衍生物并进行了结构表征。通过芳香化酶（CYP19A1）和CYP1B1抑制实验、用于雌激素受体活性的E-screen实验、乳腺癌（MCF-7 BUS、MDA-MB-231）和正常乳腺上皮（MCF-10 A）细胞中的细胞毒性实验以及用于细胞迁移的划痕实验评估了其生物活性。进行了分子对接和计算机模拟ADME分析以支持实验结果。结果：这些衍生物通过靶向雌激素信号传导的多个组分表现出显著的抗雌激素活性。一种化合物表现出强效的芳香化酶抑制作用（IC(5)(0) = 0.79微摩尔），而两种衍生物显示出强效的CYP1B1抑制作用（IC(5)(0) = 0.37微摩尔和0.71微摩尔）。在雌激素受体阳性细胞中观察到选择性细胞毒性，对正常细胞的影响较小。此外，选定的化合物显著抑制了细胞迁移。分子建模揭示了靶酶内的有利结合相互作用，ADME分析表明其具有可接受的药物样特性。结论：这些发现表明，DIM衍生物作为雌激素相关通路的选择性多靶点调节剂，可能成为激素依赖性乳腺癌治疗的有前景的辅助候选药物。
